agent_notes: Exact spelling 'Kumbhasar/कुम्भासर' almost never returns results tied to Lunkaransar/Mahajan; nearly all hits are a DIFFERENT, unrelated Kumbhasar village in Nokha tehsil (63km from Bikaner, panchayat Ratdiya, pop. 1271) — geographically wrong tehsil, flagged not our unit. Strongest lead: a 2022 Rajasthan Patrika article on the Mahajan Field Firing Range names 'कुम्भाणा' (Kumbhana) as one of the 34 acquired villages, quoting a Kumbhana-born resident (Bajrangial Lakhotia) about a surviving Holika Dahan tradition at the old site. 'Kumbhana' vs 'Kumbhasar' differ by only the final syllable (णा vs सर) — a plausible transliteration variant of the same village name from the original Facebook comment list. jatland.com has a 'Kumbhana' page (Cloudflare-blocked, only WebSearch snippet retrievable) stating it was founded by Nathu Dhatarwal's son Kumbha in Lunkaransar tehsil — this matches our unit's own geo terms 'Nathu Dada'/'Nathu Dada Dhora' and clan 'Dhatarwal' almost exactly, reinforcing that Kumbhana is likely the intended village. No hits at all in the Bikaner State/District gazetteers on archive.org, indiankanoon, YouTube, or Facebook for either spelling. GeoNames-style queries returned nothing distinct from the Nokha village. Recommend a human researcher check jatland.com/home/Kumbhana directly (blocks automated fetch) and ask Mahajan-area residents whether 'Kumbhasar' and 'Kumbhana' are the same village.
